items.title: In Break of Day, Kat Stewart and Sarah Goodes examine a universal story of poverty and progress
items.summary: Burra Creek is the home of the world's largest online retail warehouse. It's also the setting for a moving new production about the struggles faced by everyday Australian families.

items.title: The best seasonal produce to look for in August
items.summary: From baby broccoli to gai lan, these are the vegetables and fruit to look for this month.

items.title: ABC news quiz: A bored prince, Jetstar's new fee and a stunning view of… something
items.summary: Please ensure your seat is upright and, if you can still afford it, stow your bag in the overhead compartment: this quiz is ready for take-off.

items.title: US Senate committee votes to hold Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress over COVID hearing
items.summary: Dr Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination more than 100 times when he appeared before the US Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs last week.

items.title: Legend's first try in 1,426 days inspires Cowboys turnaround
items.summary: Jason Taumalolo has ended a four year try-scoring drought to inspire North Queensland to victory over Gold Coast.

items.title: Victoria Police settle lawsuit with Gippsland man left with brain damage after 2022 arrest
items.summary: A young father who suffered permanent brain damage after a Victoria Police officer fell on him during a bungled arrest in 2022 has quietly settled a lawsuit with the force in a deal believed to be worth almost $14 million.

items.title: Ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina vows to return to her country and political life. What could it mean for Bangladesh?
items.summary: In her first public appearance since fleeing to India two years ago, Bangladesh's "Iron Lady" didn't use the moment to confront the crimes for which she has been sentenced to death. Instead, she used it to signal her ongoing power as a political contender.

items.title: Roos stun Dogs to blow wildcard wide open, outrage over Cats saga
items.summary: North Melbourne ends a seven-year drought against the Western Bulldogs, as the AFL's decision not to sanction Geelong over a concussion waiver leads to more questions than answers.

items.title: High Court finds secret recording can be used as evidence in DV case
items.summary: While most recordings of private conversations are illegal, the High Court found the recording was allowed because it was necessary to protect the victim's "bodily autonomy and integrity".

items.title: Hung jury in trial of former Mount Isa priest accused of abusing boy in late 1970s
items.summary: Former Mount Isa Catholic priest Neville Joseph Creen faced a trial over allegations of child sexual abuse from the late 1970s and early '80s.

items.title: Queanbeyan's Miles Franklin Literary Award winner praises his mum, describes 'slog' of 21 drafts
items.summary: The author, poet and visual artist says his childhood was a dichotomy of Queanbeyan's suburban streets and Canberra's privileged arts scene.

items.title: WA man sentenced for 4WD crash that killed Caitlyn Bragger, injured others
items.summary: A 18-year-old has been sentenced over the 4WD crash that killed Caitlyn Bragger in 2025. Had the man not continued contesting the charges until after he turned 18, he would have been sent to juvenile detention.

items.title: ABC investigations boss leaves, as Four Corners probe continues
items.summary: The announcement comes alongside a deepening investigation into the work of sacked Four Corners reporter Mahmood Fazal. The long-running current affairs program falls under Puccini's oversight.

items.title: NT police commissioner fires back at Labor MP Luke Gosling over arrest 'politicisation' claim
items.summary: Martin Dole says a claim from Luke Gosling's lawyer that the MP's arrest was politicised is "offensive" and part of a "strategy".

items.title: Alan Jones complainant denies reporting broadcaster to police to 'get money'
items.summary: A man accusing Alan Jones of indecently assaulting him as a 17-year-old made a police complaint to "get money", the former broadcaster's lawyer has told a Sydney court.

items.title: Court fines Bucca blueberry farmers $100,000 for building an illegal dam
items.summary: The NSW Land and Environment Court fines two Mid North Coast blueberry farmers $100,000 for building an illegal dam, but they will not have to demolish it.

items.title: Stage is set for debates on tax, migration and gambling ahead of parliament's return
items.summary: Parliament is yet to resume but the stage has been set for the political fights set to play out next week.

items.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby's family sets date for funeral to honour five-year-old girl's memory
items.summary: Months on from the desperate search for five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby by hundreds of volunteers, her grandfather is inviting the community to come together once more for her funeral in Alice Springs later this month.

items.title: Climate change forces family to leave behind 'beautiful' life in Tuvalu
items.summary: As rising sea levels affect their country, many Tuvaluans, including Poeva and Akesa's family, are making the tough decision to leave.

items.title: Man convicted of killing teenager Cassius Turvey fails to reduce jail sentence
items.summary: One of the men convicted of killing Perth teenager Cassius Turvey has failed in his appeal against his nine-year jail sentence, which he claimed was "manifestly excessive".

items.title: Australian silicon producer leaving US next week after 40pc tariff imposed
items.summary: Australia's only silicon producer will exit the US market next week, but the federal government says the Trump administration's move does not undermine the critical minerals agreement between the two countries.

items.title: Sydney woman allegedly threatened to kill senior politicians, police say
items.summary: A Western Sydney woman allegedly threatened to kill NSW Labor minister Jihad Dib, One Nation leader Pauline Hanson, independent federal MP Allegra Spender and 15 others, NSW Police say.

items.title: Federal government plan to block gas-fired data centres criticised as 'overreach' by NT
items.summary: The NT government has rejected a federal plan to mandate the use of renewables for new large-scale data centres, but the Commonwealth says it will block proposals that rely on gas.

items.title: Fremantle Dockers not treating trip to the MCG any differently as finals loom
items.summary: Fremantle are flag favourites and make a rare trip this weekend to the home of the grand final — but coach Justin Longmuir isn't buying into the importance of the venue as his side looks to seal the minor premiership.

items.title: 'Terrifying' threats leading First Nations journalists to leave industry, racism inquiry hears
items.summary: Former Today show presenter Brooke Boney has told the federal racism inquiry she walked away from the industry after receiving "menacing" threats, including the doxxing of her email and home address.

items.title: NSW modern slavery report calls for urgent reform to protect migrant workers
items.summary: A NSW parliamentary inquiry into modern slavery in regional areas found evidence of migrant workers living in near-uninhabitable conditions, forced to work demanding hours and threatened if they spoke up.

items.title: Hundreds of statements being audited after typos uncovered at troubled Queensland forensics lab
items.summary: The latest bungle involved statements the lab provided to police for prosecution, which had typographical errors like the wrong date or case number. The mistake was sensationally first discovered as a scientist was in the witness box giving evidence in June.

items.title: Investigations underway into surgery mix-up at hospital in Melbourne's west
items.summary: Authorities say they are reviewing how a Melbourne woman was given surgery meant for another patient at a Sunshine hospital.

items.title: Book showcases Australia's retro television from Skippy to Hey Hey It's Saturday
items.summary: In a world of rapidly developing technology, television was once considered revolutionary. A new book by Ian Collis, Retro Television: What We Watched Back in the Day, is a nostalgic trip down memory lane.

items.title: Health regulator AHPRA apologises for breaching doctor privacy in bulk email
items.summary: The national healthcare watchdog has inadvertently identified more than 100 doctors, nurses and other practitioners who were offered addiction and alcohol misuse training in a mass email that has triggered fierce backlash and privacy complaints.

items.title: One Nation leader Pauline Hanson says she does not care if immigration cuts impact businesses
items.summary: The One Nation leader says her focus is on a "decent standard of living" and "way of life", saying she does "not care" if cuts to skilled migration will affect businesses.

items.title: ABC apologises for Race Around the World episode featuring Gina Rinehart reference
items.summary: The ABC apologises for a Race Around the World episode containing remarks about mining magnate Gina Rinehart AO, despite the broadcaster's ombudsman finding it did not breach editorial standards.

items.title: Disgraced AFL great Nicky Winmar should be jailed over assault, prosecutors say
items.summary: A Victorian court has been told the victim continues to suffer flashbacks of the attack, while a lawyer for the former AFL great says his client is being investigated for the concussion-related brain injury, CTE.

items.title: Facebook is paying controversial creators to produce rage-bait content
items.summary: An ABC NEWS Verify investigation reveals Facebook is directly funding some controversial Australian content creators including a white nationalist and an anti-vaxxer influencer.

items.title: Tattoo artists report rise of AI-generated images in customer design requests
items.summary: Tattoo artists are concerned about customers increasingly requesting designs based on AI-generated images, which they say often contain errors and set "unrealistic expectations".

items.title: Alexei Popyrin celebrates 27th birthday with straight-sets victory at Montreal Masters
items.summary: Alexei Popyrin has won for the 12th time in 13 matches at the Canadian Masters, giving himself a 27th birthday present by reached the last 32 for the third year in a row.

items.title: Telescope detects debris plume after SpaceX rocket stage crashes into Moon
items.summary: A stray piece of a rocket, the size of a school bus, has smashed into the Moon, likely creating a new crater.

items.title: Alan Jones's trial suppression on cross-examination of complainant
items.summary: One of Alan Jones's six male complainants in the veteran broadcaster's historic indecent assault trial has continued to face cross examination but a court order has limited reporting of the case.

items.title: Geelong avoids sanction from AFL over player concussion deal
items.summary: Geelong will not be penalised by the AFL for making a deal with a player who had a history of concussions that required him to assume all legal responsibility for future brain trauma.

items.title: Meta AI agent hacked external company during testing after gaining internet access, company reports
items.summary: The incident will fan concerns about how developers can contain increasingly capable AI systems, after similar incidents at rival companies Anthropic and OpenAI.

items.title: NSW drivers licence photos could be part of national database under new laws
items.summary: NSW drivers licence photos could be shared to a national database under a proposed government scheme to prevent identity fraud.

items.title: Three charged for alleged threats against judge, witnesses and officials in Nolan Wells death investigation
items.summary: Three people have been charged for allegedly threatening a US judge, authorities and witnesses connected to the investigation of Black teenager Nolan Wells's mysterious death.

items.title: Smithfield fatal crash accused Jake Edward Warn charged with manslaughter
items.summary: Accused driver Jake Edward Warn is unable to instruct a lawyer as he remains "under the influence" following a fatal crash on the northern Cairns bypass that killed 25-year-old Savannah Paige.

items.title: 100-year-old war memorial in Victorian town of Beaufort vandalised
items.summary: Locals say they are feeling hurt after a 100-year-old war memorial was vandalised with slogans including "death to Australia".

items.title: Uniform problems are just one issue that elite female athletes with body image concerns face
items.summary: Swifts netballer and professional nutritionist Teigan O'Shannassy says uniform problems are just one of the many difficulties elite female athletes struggling with body image issues face.

items.title: FIFA apologises for World Cup sell-off plan and pledges support for Infantino
items.summary: FIFA has reiterated its support for embattled president Gianni Infantino, while apologising to its member associations for the aborted bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup.

items.title: Mushroom foraging in New South Wales is legal but experts warn of deadly risks
items.summary: Foraging for mushrooms might be romantic, but experts warn assumed knowledge could be deadly.

items.title: Hopes 'innovative' mining technique can penetrate untapped mineral zone under Broken Hill
items.summary: A mining company says it has found a way to access a mineral lode discovered under Broken Hill more than 40 years ago, but once deemed too difficult to reach.

items.title: Ancient bone-crunching Territory thylacine femur uncovered near Alice Springs
items.summary: An 8-million-year-old intact femur from the bone-crunching Northern Territory tiger has been found for the first time at the Alcoota fossil beds north-east of Alice Springs.

items.title: Queensland builder fined over rust-coloured canal pollution
items.summary: An investigation by Gold Coast's council finds a builder mismanaged its dewatering program and allowed contaminated water to leak into Palm Beach's canals.

items.title: Barn owl baby boom welcomed in rural WA following mouse plague
items.summary: Clutches of barn owl chicks found inside a grain silo and cockatoo boxes indicate a "smorgasbord" of food, experts say.

items.title: Record temperatures in Austria, wildfires in Greece and Albania amid Europe heatwave
items.summary: The world's fastest-warming continent is being ravaged by record-breaking heat, wildfires and drought this summer, as well as power and water shortages.

items.title: Parental behaviour a factor in teen gambling rates, study finds
items.summary: Parental behaviour could be a significant contributing factor in teenage gambling rates, a study has found.

items.title: Royal Australian Mint releases new coin commemorating First Nations land rights
items.summary: The Royal Australian Mint is encouraging people to check their change for the new 50-cent coin.

items.title: Mount Isa's young population revels in its housing market as low prices signal buyer potential
items.summary: An outback city known for its rodeos and red dirt is home to one of the youngest average populations in Australia. With so many under 35s flocking to Mount Isa, it might be an opportunity to step into the housing market.

items.title: Woman and man found dead in Charleville, 'complex investigation' underway
items.summary: A 23-year-old woman and 45-year-old man are found dead at a property in Charleville in outback Queensland after a toddler was taken to hospital.

items.title: Court orders disability pensioner to remove 'therapeutic' roosters from regional SA property
items.summary: A disability pensioner has been ordered to remove his three consistently crowing pet roosters — which he considers to be "therapeutic animals" — from his property in regional South Australia.

items.title: New parliamentary committee to examine how Australia can prepare for war for first time since World War II
items.summary: For the first time since World War II, a formal plan will be proposed, reflecting increasing concerns about conflict breaking out in this region.

items.title: 'Marked increase' in peptide users using needle exchange facilities around Australia
items.summary: Experts and advocates fear at-risk drug users could be left without safe injecting equipment and resort to syringe sharing.

items.title: Credit default swaps at record highs signal major risk for US big tech
items.summary: Credit default swaps for US big tech companies are soaring to record highs. It means investors are fearful of a major Wall Street company collapse.

items.title: Labor could shelve gambling bill rather than accept major changes
items.summary: Labor is unlikely to entertain major changes to its gambling ad crackdown despite the bill being friendless in parliament.

items.title: Labor knows any migration program change demands careful explanation
items.summary: If stopping asylum seeker boats was the great immigration challenge in decades past, achieving a lower Net Overseas Migration (NOM) figure has become the new political test.

items.title: Carnival cruise workers make 'horrifying' allegations about conditions
items.summary: Passengers boarding a Carnival cruise ship are promised a world of endless food, relaxation and oceanic luxury. But for the crew who make these escapes possible, life is vastly different.
